featuredPapers.title: Intranasal Versus Intramuscular Midazolam in Pediatric Seizure Control: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
featuredPapers.summary: Meta-analysis testing whether intranasal or intramuscular midazolam works better for paediatric seizures without cannula access — intramuscular midazolam was associated with faster seizure termination and less need for rescue therapy, especially in the prehospital setting.
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Directly informs prehospital seizure management when IV access isn't available — IM may be better than intranasal for rapid control.

featuredPapers.title: Paramedics' decisions to withhold resuscitation in traumatic cardiac arrest: accuracy of paramedic assessments compared with autopsy findings
featuredPapers.summary: Retrospective Ontario review testing how paramedics decide to withhold CPR in traumatic cardiac arrest — most no-CPR decisions were based on signs clearly incompatible with life, and post-mortem findings supported paramedic assessment in the large majority of cases.
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Validates paramedic judgment in withholding CPR for traumatic cardiac arrest — most clinical assessments align with autopsy findings.

featuredPapers.title: Out-of-Hospital Management of Suspected Spinal Cord Injuries: How Much Evidence Does It Take to Change Practice?
featuredPapers.summary: Commentary challenging continued routine spinal immobilisation in suspected spinal injury — the authors argue decades of evidence now consistently show harm without benefit, and that paramedic scope should evolve to reflect current evidence.
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Questions a routine prehospital practice — decades of evidence suggest spinal immobilisation may cause more harm than benefit.

featuredPapers.title: Factors associated with hospital transport in emergency medical services-attended out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
featuredPapers.summary: Retrospective cohort of 3339 OHCA patients found 68.9% were not transported, with transport more likely in witnessed arrests, bystander CPR, hypertension, and shorter time from last known normal, and less likely with older age, malignancy, prior stroke, and arrests at home.
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Large cohort clarifies which OHCA patients get transported — helps understand transport decision patterns in real-world practice.

featuredPapers.title: Utilization and Metrics Associated with Paramedic Treat and Discharge Medical Directives for Paramedic Services and Emergency Departments: A Retrospective Cohort Study
featuredPapers.summary: This retrospective cohort study analysed paramedic treat and discharge medical directives to understand utilisation patterns and key metrics for prehospital and emergency department decision-making — the findings provide valuable insights into the scope, safety, and operational impact of treat-and-refer pathways.
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Examines treat-and-refer pathways — growing in importance as paramedic scope expands to manage patients at home.

papers.title: Feasibility and agreement of a self-adhesive EEG electrode set versus conventional EEG in postanoxic coma
papers.summary: Comparison of forehead EEG electrodes versus conventional EEG in 51 postanoxic coma patients found forehead recordings were interpretable in 74.1% of cases with moderate agreement, suggesting potential as a screening tool to reduce technician workload.

papers.title: Emergency Medicine Residents in the Prehospital Setting: Does This Augment Training?
papers.summary: Five-year retrospective of a physician response vehicle staffed by EM residents found residents gained valuable exposure to adult and paediatric cardiac arrests, refusals, death pronouncements, and critical trauma, with an average of 28-79 encounters per resident.

papers.title: Can a Large Language Model Grounded in Text-Based Agency-Specific Prehospital Protocols Provide Accurate Care Recommendations?
papers.summary: This study tested whether a large language model trained on agency-specific prehospital protocol documents could generate accurate care recommendations — they found promising accuracy for protocol interpretation and clinical decision support, suggesting potential for LLMs to assist with guideline navigation at the point of care.

papers.title: Predictive Value of Carotid Artery Doppler Ultrasound for Resuscitation Outcomes in Patients with Cardiac Arrest
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine

papers.title: Eye-related emergency calls and prehospital management in region Zealand, Danmark: a register-based cohort study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Register-based cohort of 340 eye-related emergency calls found chemical exposures (31.5%), vision loss (25.9%), and trauma (18.2%) as leading causes, with 11.5% of patients initially coded for eye problems later diagnosed with stroke.

papers.title: Prophylaxis of opioid-induced nausea in helicopter emergency medical service: a prospective quasi-experimental study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Prospective study of 205 HEMS patients comparing ondansetron prophylaxis, aromatherapy, and no prophylaxis for opioid-induced nausea — neither intervention showed benefit compared to no prophylaxis in unselected patients.

papers.title: Manual versus Automated Ventilation with an i-gel® Airway During Short-Haul Helicopter Operations
papers.summary: Simulation study comparing bag-valve ventilation with automated ventilation during short-haul helicopter rescue using an i-gel — automated ventilation achieved target minute ventilation more consistently, caused less airway movement, and avoided disconnects.

papers.title: The role of tactical police medics in the prehospital environment: results from an interview study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Interview study exploring how Swedish tactical police medics view their training, role, and real-world practice — they reported being well trained but underused, with scope restrictions and inconsistent collaboration limiting what they can actually do.

papers.title: The impact of advanced pre-hospital interventions on scene time
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective physician-led HEMS trauma study examining whether more advanced interventions are stretching scene times — each additional intervention increased scene time by 41%, although overall scene times stayed similar over two decades because of changing case mix.

papers.title: Out-of-Hospital Management of Suspected Spinal Cord Injuries: How Much Evidence Does it Take to Change Practice?
papers.summary: Commentary challenging continued routine spinal immobilisation in suspected spinal injury — the authors argue decades of evidence now consistently show harm without benefit, and that paramedic scope should evolve to reflect current evidence.

papers.title: Early Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction After Intracerebral Hemorrhage Is Associated With Worse Functional Outcome: The Risk of Overshooting Blood Pressure Goals
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort testing whether rapid systolic BP reduction ≤150 mm Hg after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage improved outcomes — early target achievement and overshooting <120 mm Hg were associated with worse functional outcome.

papers.title: No delayed intracranial hemorrhage in head injury patients on oral anticoagulants and with normal CT: a retrospective study of 215 patients
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective review tested whether immediate discharge after normal CT was safe for anticoagulated head-injury patients with GCS 14–15 — no delayed intracranial haemorrhage, neurosurgical intervention, or clinically significant deterioration occurred.

papers.title: Comparison of needle decompression to simple (finger) thoracostomy in non-perfused cadaveric models with theoretical tension pneumothorax
papers.summary: Cadaveric crossover study testing needle decompression versus simple thoracostomy for theoretical tension pneumothorax — simple thoracostomy was more successful and faster, but the model limits clinical certainty.

papers.title: Healthcare costs of expedited transport compared with standard care following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: results from the EVIDENCE randomised controlled trial
papers.summary: Greater Sydney costing analysis of expedited OHCA transport for possible ECPR versus standard care — overall health system costs were comparable, with higher costs when patients arrived during ECPR business hours.

papers.title: Effect of vascular access strategy on long-term outcomes in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a randomised clinical trial
papers.summary: IVIO follow-up comparing initial intraosseous versus intravenous access in adult non-traumatic OHCA — 6-month and 1-year outcomes were similar, with no evidence that either access strategy improves long-term survival or neurological outcome.

papers.title: Feasibility of portable telemedicine devices for ambulance-based prehospital triage: a comparative simulation study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Simulation study comparing portable telemedicine devices for ambulance triage, and found the Vuzix headset ranked highest overall, but the smartphone app was the most practical early implementation option.

papers.title: The Estimated Benefit of Lights and Sirens During Ambulance Transport
papers.summary: This study used a modern transport model to estimate whether lights and sirens save time, and it found a median gain of only 3.0 to 3.3 minutes per trip, which likely does not justify the known driving risks except in selected cases.

The impact of defibrillation current and pad position on return of spontaneous circulation during refractory ventricular fibrillation
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of DOSE VF examined whether transthoracic current, pad position, and ROSC were linked, and found AP pad placement delivered higher current and was independently associated with ROSC, while delivered current itself was not.

papers.title: Feasibility of portable telemedicine devices for ambulance-based prehospital triage: a comparative simulation study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Simulation study comparing portable telemedicine devices for ambulance triage, and found the Vuzix headset ranked highest overall, but the smartphone app was the most practical early implementation option.

papers.title: The diamond minutes: rethinking the earliest link of the trauma chain of survival
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Concept editorial arguing that the first minutes after injury, before EMS arrival, are a distinct high-risk window where bystander action and dispatcher guidance can prevent deaths, especially through haemorrhage control and airway management.

papers.title: Introduction of a Clinical Practice Guideline for Patella Reduction by Paramedics: The Effect on Pain Relief, Relocation, and Transport Decision
papers.summary: They tested whether Ambulance Victoria's patella-reduction guideline improved analgesia and service outcomes, and found no analgesia gain but fewer cannulae, fewer transports, and shorter cases.

papers.title: The Effect of Lights and Sirens on Critical Care Transport Time
papers.summary: They measured whether lights and sirens meaningfully shorten critical care transport, and found a statistically significant but modest time saving of about 8 minutes.

papers.title: Feasibility of a Pre-Hospital Virtual Triage and Care Model: A Mixed-Methods Pilot in Emergency Care
papers.summary: They tested a pre-hospital telehealth model for ambulance-retrieved patients, and found it was feasible, advanced senior review, and reduced ED length of stay without improving crew cycle times.

papers.title: Sonorheometry to detect traumatic induced coagulopathy during initial management of trauma patients: an observational, multi-center study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Tested whether Quantra can rapidly detect trauma-induced coagulopathy against standard lab tests, and found early Quantra analysis may reliably exclude TIC, but prospective validation is still needed.

papers.title: Chest X-Ray evaluation using GPT for tube thoracostomy or conservative care in non-tension spontaneous pneumothorax
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Tested whether a vision-enabled GPT model could estimate pneumothorax size and guide tube thoracostomy vs conservative care, and it matched radiologist measurements closely with good agreement to real-world ED decisions.

papers.title: Paramedic Patella Reduction — Ambulance Victoria CPG Evaluation
papers.summary: Retrospective study (n=1,210) evaluating whether Ambulance Victoria's Nov 2022 CPG for paramedic patella reduction changed practice — 91.8% reduction success rate, transport rate dropped 38.4%, case duration cut by ~33 minutes, and IV cannula use down 17.3%, with no change in effective analgesia rates.

papers.title: Delayed Defibrillation of Ventricular Arrhythmias During Transcutaneous Pacing
papers.summary: Case series examining the problem of ventricular arrhythmias occurring during TCP and delays to defibrillation — highlights the clinical trap of pacing artefact masking VF and the need to pause pacing to identify shockable rhythms.

tldr.summary:
• IM midazolam may beat intranasal for rapid paediatric seizure control without cannula.
• Paramedic no-CPR decisions in traumatic cardiac arrest align with autopsy findings in most cases.
• Commentary questions routine spinal immobilisation — decades of evidence suggest more harm than benefit.
• Two-thirds of OHCA patients aren't transported; transport more likely with witnessed arrests and bystander CPR.
• Ondansetron and aromatherapy don't prevent opioid-induced nausea better than no prophylaxis.
• Study finds median lights-and-sirens time saving only 3 minutes per trip.

highlights.note: IM midazolam achieved faster seizure termination than intranasal in prehospital paediatric seizures.

highlights.title: Traumatic Cardiac Arrest — Withholding CPR
highlights.note: Paramedic clinical judgment in withholding resuscitation matched post-mortem findings in most cases.

highlights.title: Spinal Immobilisation Under Scrutiny
highlights.note: Decades of evidence consistently show spinal immobilisation causes harm without benefit.

highlights.title: Transport Patterns in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
highlights.note: Witnessed arrests and bystander CPR increase likelihood of transport in OHCA.

highlights.title: Treat-and-Discharge Pathways
highlights.note: Retrospective analysis provides insights into scope and safety of paramedic treat-and-refer pathways.
